entries.q: How much does roof replacement cost in Columbus, OH?
entries.a: Cost depends on square footage, roof pitch, the number of roof planes, the condition of the decking once the old roof is off, and the system you choose. Anyone quoting a firm number over the phone without seeing the roof is guessing. We measure and give you a written, line-itemed scope so you can see exactly what drives the price.

entries.q: Does Roof King offer roof financing?
entries.a: Yes. We work with third-party lenders including Hearth and Medallion Bank, with 3-year and 5-year terms available. Approval, rate and term are set by the lender based on your credit, not by us. Ask for the APR and the total paid over the full term before you sign anything.

entries.q: Does homeowners insurance cover storm damage roof repair?
entries.a: Insurance covers sudden accidental damage such as hail and wind. It does not cover wear, age or deferred maintenance. Whether your specific loss is covered depends on your policy and the damage present, which is why we document the roof thoroughly before advising you on a claim.

entries.q: How can I spot storm damage on my roof?
entries.a: From the ground, look for missing or lifted shingles, granules collecting in gutters and downspouts, dents on gutters, downspouts, vents and soft metals, and any new staining on ceilings or at exterior walls. Hail bruising often is not visible from the ground at all, which is why we mark and photograph test squares on every slope.

entries.q: Do you install gutter guards?
entries.a: Yes. Gutter guards are worth the money on homes under real tree cover and close to pointless on an open lot, and we will tell you which one you have. We install in a way that does not compromise a GAF system warranty.

entries.q: Can Roof King help with ice dam removal?
entries.a: Yes, using low-pressure steam. Chipping ice off a roof breaks shingles and a hot pressure washer strips granules. We also look at why the dam formed, because ice dams are an attic heat loss and ventilation issue rather than a roof covering issue.

entries.q: What are common signs of roof damage?
entries.a: Missing, cracked or curling shingles, granules in the gutters, damaged or lifted flashing, daylight or staining visible in the attic, sagging areas, and interior water spots. Any of these is worth an inspection before the next storm rather than after it.

entries.q: How long does a roof replacement take?
entries.a: Most residential roof replacements are a single day on the roof. Larger, steeper or more complex homes run two to three days. We confirm the schedule before material is dropped, and we never tear off more than we can dry in before the crew leaves.

entries.q: Do you provide emergency roof repair?
entries.a: Yes. Active leaks and storm emergencies move to the front of the schedule. Call the office rather than filling out a form if water is coming in right now and we will get you tarped and scheduled.

entries.q: What areas does Roof King serve?
entries.a: We work statewide in Ohio from our Columbus office, with the heaviest coverage in Columbus, Dayton, Cincinnati, Cleveland and Akron and the communities around them. If your city is not listed on our service areas page, call and ask.

entries.q: Is this the same as a hail report an adjuster uses?
entries.a: It overlaps but it is not identical. Carriers often buy radar-derived products that estimate hail size across a grid rather than at reported points. Those are modelled estimates. NOAA reports are observed reports. Both are used in claims, and an observed report on a specific date is generally the harder of the two to argue with.

entries.q: My address shows nothing. Does that mean my roof is fine?
entries.a: No. It means nobody filed a report within fifteen miles in that period. Hail bands are narrow and rural areas in particular get under-reported because there is nobody there to report. If your shingles are showing granule loss, bruising or mat fracture, the roof is telling you something the database does not know.

entries.q: Will checking my address start a claim or put me on a list?
entries.a: No. Looking up a date does nothing to your policy and nothing to your rates. We do not submit anything anywhere on your behalf, and we do not sell or share what you type here.

entries.q: How far back does it go?
entries.a: January 2019 to the most recent NOAA publication. Ohio only. Most carriers have a reporting window measured in months to a year from the date of loss, so events older than that are usually historical context rather than a live claim.

entries.q: How long does a roof last in Ohio?
entries.a: Architectural asphalt shingles are commonly rated 25 to 30 years, but actual service life in Ohio depends far more on attic ventilation than on the shingle. A well ventilated roof reaches its rating. A poorly ventilated one frequently does not make it two thirds of the way.

entries.q: Do I need a full replacement or just a repair?
entries.a: Repair is right when the roof has meaningful life left and the failure is isolated, such as a single storm-damaged slope or a flashing detail. Replacement is right when the field of the roof is at end of life, when there are multiple existing layers, or when repair costs are approaching a meaningful fraction of replacement. We will tell you which one you have.

entries.q: Will my insurance cover a new roof?
entries.a: Insurance covers sudden accidental damage such as hail and wind. It does not cover wear, age or deferred maintenance. Whether your specific loss is covered depends on your policy and the damage present, which is why we document first and advise second.

entries.q: Can you waive or cover my deductible?
entries.a: No. Waiving, absorbing or rebating an insurance deductible is illegal in Ohio and exposes the homeowner as well as the contractor. Any contractor offering it is telling you something important about how they operate.

entries.q: Do you pull permits?
entries.a: Yes, under our license, and we coordinate the inspection with the authority having jurisdiction for your address. A contractor asking you to pull an owner permit for their work is shifting liability onto you.

entries.q: How long does the work take?
entries.a: Most residential roof replacements are one day on the roof. Steeper, larger or more complex homes run two to three. Siding and deck projects are typically several days to a week or more depending on scope.

entries.q: What happens to my landscaping and driveway?
entries.a: We tarp and protect landscaping, use plywood over sensitive drive surfaces where needed, and run a magnet over the property for nails at the end of each day and again at completion. If we damage something, we fix it.

entries.q: Do you work in winter?
entries.a: Roofing yes, with attention to temperature since asphalt shingles need warmth to seal properly and some products have installation temperature limits. Vinyl siding becomes brittle in deep cold. We will tell you honestly if your specific project should wait for spring rather than taking the deposit.

entries.q: Are you licensed and insured?
entries.a: Yes. License HIC-L00828 through the City of Columbus, plus an active Ohio general contractor license, general liability and workers compensation. Ask us for certificates before work begins. Ask every bidder for the same.

entries.q: What is the difference between Master Elite and a regular GAF contractor?
entries.a: Any contractor can buy and install GAF shingles. Master Elite is a certification GAF grants to a small percentage of contractors, and it is what permits us to write the GAF System Plus and Golden Pledge Limited Warranty. Without it, a contractor simply cannot offer those, regardless of what their proposal implies.

entries.q: Do you offer financing?
entries.a: We work with third-party lenders including Hearth and Medallion Bank. Approval, rate and term are set by the lender based on your credit, not by us. See our financing page for what to ask before you sign anything.

entries.q: What warranty comes with the roof?
entries.a: Every installation carries our 5-year workmanship warranty. As a GAF Master Elite contractor we can also offer GAF System Plus and the Golden Pledge Limited Warranty on qualifying systems, which extends coverage well beyond what a non-certified contractor can write.

entries.q: Do you handle the permit?
entries.a: Yes. We pull the permit under our license and coordinate inspection with the authority having jurisdiction for your address.

entries.q: What happens if it rains mid-job?
entries.a: We do not tear off more than we can dry in. Open deck gets covered and secured before crews leave the property, every day.

entries.q: What if my claim was already denied?
entries.a: A denial can be reinspected. Bring us the carrier estimate, the denial letter and the loss date. We review the file against what is actually on the roof before advising you on next steps.

entries.q: Will a claim raise my rates?
entries.a: That is between you and your carrier and we will not speculate about your policy. Your agent can tell you how weather-related claims are treated on your specific policy.

entries.q: Can you waive my deductible?
entries.a: No, and no reputable Ohio contractor will. A contractor offering that is telling you what they are willing to do to your insurer, and eventually to you.

entries.q: Do you replace the wrap underneath?
entries.a: Yes. Siding replacement includes inspecting and correcting the water-resistive barrier and flashings. That is the part that actually keeps water out.

entries.q: Do guards void anything?
entries.a: Some guard systems fastened under the shingle course can affect a roof warranty depending on the manufacturer. We install in a way that does not compromise a GAF system warranty.

entries.q: Can you rebuild just the surface?
entries.a: Sometimes. If the framing and ledger are sound, re-decking is a legitimate option and we will say so. If the ledger detail is wrong, surfacing over it is spending money on the wrong layer.

entries.q: Do you do maintenance agreements?
entries.a: Yes. Scheduled inspection and minor repair on a low-slope roof is materially cheaper than reactive replacement.

entries.a: Yes. We hold license HIC-L00828 issued by the City of Columbus plus an active Ohio general contractor license, and we pull permits under our license with the authority having jurisdiction for your specific address.

entries.a: Non-emergency inspections are generally scheduled within a few business days. Active leaks and storm damage move to the front. Call (614) 379-8893 rather than using the form if water is coming in right now.
